universalAnswers.whatHappened: Nature reported that five drug companies pooled 20,167 private protein-ligand structures to fine-tune a research AI model.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A reported research-model comparison rather than a medicine, trial, approval or patient outcome.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: One complete captured Nature report with the stated consortium numbers and limitations.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: The model is not public and the described study has not been peer reviewed.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: Readers can separate a better model test result from a claim that a treatment works.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: No patient group, prescription, product user or care change is identified.
universalAnswers.changesNow: No medicine, clinical result or public model release is reported.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Whether this reported benchmark will lead to validated drugs remains unknown.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Ask whether an AI-drug headline describes a model, a tested drug or a patient outcome.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: What stage of evidence does this headline actually report?

research-benchmark.researchQuestion: The report asks whether private protein-ligand structures can improve predictions on held-out structures.
research-benchmark.method: The consortium fine-tuned an OpenFold3-based model and compared prediction accuracy on examples kept outside training.
research-benchmark.result: Nature reports the private-data model predicted more held-out protein-molecule structures accurately than public-data comparisons.
research-benchmark.sponsorAndInterests: Five drug companies supplied proprietary structures and therefore have a direct research interest in the reported model improvement.
research-benchmark.independentReplication: Nature reports the described study has not been peer reviewed, so no independent replication is established here.
research-benchmark.realWorldTransfer: A held-out structure benchmark can guide research but does not establish a treatment works in people.
research-benchmark.limitations: The model is not public, the study is unreviewed and no clinical or patient outcome is reported.

translation.newsVersionExact: This is a research-model comparison, not an announcement of a new drug.
translation.actualMeaningExact: A model benchmark asks whether a system makes better predictions.
translation.mechanismExact: A held-out test uses examples kept separate from training.
translation.familiarExampleExact: Ask whether a later headline reports a model, a tested drug, or a patient outcome.
